faq.a: Beyza is associated with the Arabic form بَيْضَاء, whose core sense is beyza; white, bright (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Beyza?
faq.a: Beyza is associated with Arabic. Beyza is the Turkish form of Arabic بَيْضَاء (Bayḍāʾ), the feminine of أَبْيَض, meaning 'white, bright'.
Yes — the underlying form بَيْضَاء is Arabic.
Beyza can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Beyza should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Bayḍāʾ is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: In Urdu, Beyza is rendered بیضاء and carries the sense بیضاء، سفید.

faq.q: What does Beyza mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Beyza is rendered بیضا and carries the sense بیضا، سپید.
A romanized syllable approximation is bey-za. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Beyza?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Beyza, beyza. Script forms are بيضاء, بَيْضَاء, بیضا, بیضاء, बैज़ा.

faq.q: Is Beyza a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
